full_judgment:
4. Heard Mr. Syed Ziaul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant and Mr. MA Rouf, Assistant Attorney-General who opposes the appeal on behalf of the State Mr. Ziaul Karim has assailed the trial Court's order of conviction and sentence on the ground that the trial was held by a Special Tribunal as it appears from the judgment and order sheet of the court. The Special Tribunal, according to him, constituted under the Special Powers Act, 1974, is not competent to try a case under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and therefore the trial is vitiated for want of competence. His second contention is that in the charge there was no mention of the date or dates between which the alleged offence of breach of trust was committed by the accused and from the deposition it appears that it was alleged by the prosecution that the breach of trust took place within a span of 3 years and, therefore, the charge as framed by the court below is repugnant to the provision of section 234 CrPC. The third contention is that the accused appellant was not properly examined under section 342 CrPC resulting in his being prejudiced which has vitiated the trial. His last contention it that the conviction is not warranted by the evidence on record so far as the allegation of misappropriation is concerned. 

 6. It appears that in the heading of the impugned judgment the court concerned has been described as Special Tribunal Court, Bhola and at the bottom of the judgment and order under the signature of the judge the designation Special Tribunal, Bhola has been stated. So it appears that the case was tried by the Assistant Sessions Judge Mr. Akramuzzaman Bhuiya as a Special Tribunal and not as a Special Judge. A Special Tribunal is not competent to try a case under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 read with the provision of the. Prevention of Corruption Act 1947 But it appears that the Sessions Judge took cognizance in his capacity as Senior Special Judge and the case was numbered as a Special Case No. 7/85. So it appears that the Assistant Sessions Judge either out of ignorance or due to his callousness signed the judgment as Special Tribunal. But the accused-appellant has not been prejudiced in any manner whatsoever. Soon this ground alone there cannot be any question of the trial to be vitiated for want of competence. 

 9. Moreover, it also appears that in imposing fine of Taka 300.00 the learned Trying Court violated the mandatory provision of section 9 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 by imposing a token fine which is much less than the amount of misappropriation of Taka 61,000.00 and odds.
